title: Irrigation start-up and winterization guide

seo.title: Irrigation start-up and winterizing in Victoria, BC
seo.description: When and how to start up and winterize an irrigation system on southern Vancouver Island, with a zone checklist and the CRD lawn days to set.

summary: A spring start-up checklist and a fall shutdown guide for home and strata irrigation systems.

body.p: Freezing nights are not frequent here, but one hard frost can crack pipes and valves in a system full of water. A proper fall shutdown and a careful spring start-up prevent most repairs.

list: Open the main supply slowly to avoid pressure surges.
Run each zone and look for leaks, broken heads and dry spots.
Adjust heads so they water plants, not paths or buildings.
Replace the controller battery and check the clock.
Set lawn zones to your CRD days and times before May 1.
Turn off the controller or set it to off or rain mode.
Shut off the supply to the system.
Drain the system, or have it blown out with compressed air by someone with the right equipment.
Insulate exposed pipes and the backflow assembly where applicable.

body.p: Many irrigation systems have a backflow preventer that protects drinking water. Ask your water supplier whether your assembly needs testing.

list: Convert shrub and flower beds from spray to drip.
Add a rain or soil-moisture sensor.
Use a smart controller that adjusts to weather.

body.p: Book start-up or winterization through [irrigation services](/services/irrigation/), read the [CRD watering rules guide](/resources/crd-watering-rules-guide/), or [get a free quote](/free-quote/).
